prompt:
You are a senior fashion designer at a high-street retailer, designing a new product for the Autumn 2020 collection.

STYLE TO DESIGN FOR: Ladieswear · Skirt · Solid · Black · Dark tone

The attached photos are this style's best-selling articles, in this order:
1. Tuby skirt: Short, fitted skirt in jersey with an elasticated waist.
2. Florida skirt: Pleated, calf-length skirt in woven fabric with a high, elasticated waist. Unlined.
3. Cezanne: Calf-length skirt in a textured weave. High waist with covered elastication, a seam at the thighs and a flare to the hem. Lined.
4. Libra skirt: Short skirt in a softly draping weave with a high waist and detachable tie belt. Concealed zip at the back, side pockets and pleats at the top to create soft draping. Unlined.
5. Tangerine: Long, high-waisted skirt in a viscose weave with covered elastication at the waist and gathered seams creating tiers at the thighs and knees for added width. Unlined.

Study every photo and description closely: silhouette, length, fit, waistband or neckline, closures, seams, fabric,
texture, weight and drape, hems and finishing details. Identify the visual ideas they share.

Then design ONE new skirt for Autumn 2020:
- Stay within the style: Ladieswear, skirt, solid, black, dark tone.
- KEEP the strongest visual ideas the best sellers share.
- CHANGE something meaningful for Autumn 2020 (silhouette, length, construction details, fabric or texture), so it
  is a genuinely new product and not a copy of any best seller.
- Keep it realistic to produce at high-street prices.

Be very specific and concrete: a pattern maker must be able to draw it, and an image generator must be able to render it
exactly. Use measurable or visual terms (e.g. "hem 8 cm below the knee", "5 cm wide rib-knit waistband"), not vague ones.

Answer as JSON with exactly these keys:
"name": 2-4 word product name,
"keeps": list of 2-4 visual ideas taken from the best sellers, each saying which best seller(s) it comes from,
"changes": list of 2-4 design changes for Autumn 2020, each saying why it suits the season,
"description": one sentence for a merchandiser,
"design_details": object with these keys, each 1-3 detailed sentences:
    "silhouette_and_fit", "length_and_proportions", "waist_neckline_and_closures", "fabric_and_weight",
    "texture_and_surface", "construction_and_seams", "details_and_trims", "hem_and_finishing", "colour_and_finish",
"visual_description": a 150-250 word paragraph describing exactly what the garment looks like, from top to bottom,
"image_prompt": a 60-110 word prompt for a text-to-image model that describes the garment's look precisely (start with
    the colour and garment type, name every visible detail) and ends with: "flat lay e-commerce catalogue photograph of the single garment, photographed from directly above, on a plain light grey background, soft even studio lighting, sharp fabric detail, no person, no model, no mannequin, no other items, no text, no logo".
